newsitem.title: PERU: LIMA SHARES CLOSE WITH GAINS, BOOSTED BY ADRS.
newsitem.headline: LIMA SHARES CLOSE WITH GAINS, BOOSTED BY ADRS.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange made healthy gains Thursday, as local investors traded the stocks with best long-term profitability prospects and Peruvian ADRs recovered in New York, brokers said.
They added that the bolsa should maintain the same tendency or be stable Friday, although corrections were expected for the beginning of next week.

Thursday, the General Index rose 1.23 percent to 2063.45 points as the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 1.22 percent to 2965.29 points. In a total of 1,556 transactions, volume was 36 million soles ($13.7 million).

"Investors are buying in the brewery, construction and telecommunications sector," said Manuel Torres of local Finvest brokerage. "These stocks are the leaders of the market, have low prices and have good long-term prospects."
He added that most of Thursday's players were local investors, with foreigners staying in more profitable markets, like Mexico.
"The New York rise of benchmark Telefonica del Peru's ADRs was an incentive for other local stocks to rise," added Hernando Pastor of T&J brokerage.
Telefonica del Peru rose 1.76 percent to 6.35 soles on volume of 2.1 million shares traded.

Among leaders, miner Volcan rose 6.61 percent to 25 soles on volume of 142,000 shares. Miner Buenaventura's common shares rose 3.11 percent to 23.20 soles on volume of 110,000 shares, and its labor shares rose five percent to 21.00 soles on volume of 17,001 shares.
Food company Alicorp rose 6.56 percent to 3.90 soles on volume of 17,446 shares and candy-producer D'Onofrio climbed 3.88 percent to 1.07 soles on volume of 105,000 shares.

Electricity producer Edegel and distributor Edelnor recovered some of the week's losses by rising 2.91 percent to 1.06 soles on volume of 832,000 shares and 3.61 percent to 1.72 soles on volume of 136,000 shares, respectively.

Thursday's big loser among leaders was miner Morococha, with a 3.18 percent drop to 6.70 soles on volume of 126,000 shares, followed by another miner, Milpo which fell 1.22 percent to 36.55 soles on volume of 23,258 shares traded.
